title: How large a crowd a raider needs

thesis.claim: A raider needs a crowd. In worlds 2 and 3 of Experiment 16 at iteration 2,000, the share of plantings in which a patch of raiders takes hold rises with the patch: none of the 20 single raiders takes hold, and at least half of the 20 patches of 5% do. A planting takes hold when, after 300 iterations, its raiders are alive, more than the patch began with, and more than the control holds there: the same patch given frozen copies of one resident's brain.
thesis.why: In Chapter 51 a patch of 5% of raiders took 40% and 50% of world 2 and 62% of world 3, while a single raider died out in all 20 plantings in world 2, with peaks of up to 28 agents. Its play pays only with three things at once: the raid, the password and enough teammates (the green beard). Chapter 94's replay of the same patches lost one of four in worlds 2 and 3 to chance. Twenty plantings of each size, ten places in each world, bound how often a size could take hold and be missed: none in 20 still allows up to 14% at 95% confidence.
thesis.confirm: No single raider of 20 takes hold, at least 10 of the 20 patches of 5% do, and no smaller patch takes hold in three or more plantings in twenty more than a larger one.
thesis.refute: A single raider takes hold, fewer than 10 of the 20 patches of 5% do, or a smaller patch takes hold in three or more plantings in twenty more than a larger one.
